sentences.text: The app came in about 2016 and it is a good app.

It does the astronomy properly and it also pulls a surge model from the national service, which means it does have the weather in it — a forecast of it, on a grid, updated four times a day — and it is right about the water at Kerlouan very nearly all of the time.
The reading died in about four years.
Maëlle can date it, roughly, from who stopped coming to the wall.
Four men stopped in 2017.
Two more in 2019.
Her grandfather went out every day until the September he was seventy-nine, and after that only when there was weather in it, which is what she does now.
Nobody decided to stop.
There was no argument and nobody in that harbour ever said that the fish were nonsense.

What happened is that a thing which took forty years to learn and ninety minutes of standing on a wall was replaced by a thing that took no time and required nothing, and it was right, and the men who could read the shoal got old.
That is the whole mechanism and Maëlle has stopped being angry about it, because when she is honest she cannot construct the argument for the other outcome.
What was anybody supposed to have done?
Told a twenty-two-year-old with a mortgage to spend forty years learning a skill in order to be occasionally slightly better than a free app?
The reading was not lost through carelessness.
It was outcompeted, fairly, by something that works.
By the time Maëlle was twelve there were two: her grandfather, who was eighty-one, and a man called Le Guen who did not come down to the harbour any more.

She learned it because her grandfather was dying and because she was the only person in the family who would sit on that wall for ninety minutes, and she is entirely clear that she learned it for the wrong reason and got it by accident.
He did not set out to teach her.
He set out to go and look at the fish, which he had done nearly every day of his life, and he could not get down the wall on his own by then and Maëlle was twelve and had nothing else on.
So she went with him.
And he talked, because he had always talked, and about four months in she said something about the shoal being higher than yesterday and he stopped walking.
It took eleven months.
She was not good at it.

She is still not good at it — her grandfather could call the water to about fifteen centimetres and Maëlle, at twenty-four, can call it to about forty, which is the difference between forty years and eleven months.

He died in the October and she went out on the wall on the day of the funeral because she could not think what else to do with the afternoon, and the shoal was strung out down the channel and holding deep, and the water that evening was under the table by about thirty centimetres, and she got it right and there was nobody to tell.
